transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope it's okay that I'm here, I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in. 

I guess... well, things have been a little stressful at my job. I'm a retail buyer, and what really made me come in is that I've been having this feeling lately that I just can't shake. I really don't want to sound crazy or anything, but I keep feeling like people at work, and maybe even some of our vendors, are tracking my buys. Like they're purposely messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. 

I know how that sounds, I really do. My supervisor even sat down and showed me the reports to prove that it isn't happening, and I want to believe him so I can just be a good employee, but... I still feel like they're doing it. Is that... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things okay.
Do you think these people are tracking your buys for a specific reason?

Well, um, kind of like I was just saying... I really think it's just to make me look stupid. I hate saying that out loud because I don't want to sound like I'm accusing people or being a difficult employee. I try really hard to get along with everyone, I promise. 

But it just feels like they're purposely messing with those launch numbers so I fail. And I know my supervisor showed me the reports, and I nodded and agreed with him when we met because I want to be a team player... but honestly, I just still can't shake the feeling that they're doing it to make me look incompetent. 

I hope it's okay to admit that here. I don't want you to think I'm just being paranoid or causing drama at work. Am I making sense?
Do you think people are talking about you or your work when you're not around?

Um... no, not really. I don't think they're talking about me behind my back or anything like that. I mean, I hope they aren't. I try to be really friendly with everyone in the office, and I'd like to think we all get along okay for the most part. 

It's really just that feeling about the numbers, you know? But as far as people gossiping or whispering about me when I leave the room... no, I haven't noticed anything like that. Does that help? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you still believe that people are tracking your buys and messing with the launch numbers, even after your supervisor showed you the reports?

Um... yeah. I mean, I really wish I didn't. I know he showed me the papers, and I really tried to just accept it because I want to be a good employee and not cause any trouble. But... yeah, honestly, I just can't shake it. 

I still feel like they're tracking my buys and messing with the numbers to make me look stupid. Even some of the vendors. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds so stubborn of me, and I really don't mean to be. I just... the feeling is still there, no matter what the reports say. I hope you don't think I'm just being difficult by admitting that? I really am trying my best to just do my job well.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear?

Um... well... I really hesitate to say yes to that, because I don't want you to think I'm crazy. I promise I'm a really normal guy otherwise, and I work really hard. But... I guess, sometimes? Just occasionally. 

Like, if I'm alone in the stockroom at work, or if I'm driving back from a vendor meeting, I'll hear this man's voice. It sounds like it's coming from right behind me, and he'll say something like, "Move faster, Scott," or he'll just start laughing at the items I picked. And then I turn around to see who it is, and... nobody is there. 

I usually just try to shake it off and focus on my job, because I really want to do good work and not let it distract me. Is it... is it bad that I hear that? I hope you don't think I'm totally losing my mind or anything for admitting it.
Do you find it hard to organize your thoughts or express them in a way that makes sense to others?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I hope I'm making sense right now? I always try really hard to be clear when I'm talking to people, especially at work. I want to make sure I'm doing a good job and that everyone understands what I'm trying to say about the orders and stuff. 

I don't think anyone has ever told me I'm hard to understand or that my thoughts are all jumbled up. I try to stay really organized, you know? Both with my work and just... how I talk. Does it seem like I'm making sense to you? I really hope I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do you still think people are tracking your buys and messing with the launch numbers every day?

Um... yeah, I guess it is pretty much every day. I really hate to admit that, because I want to tell you I'm doing better and not make a big deal out of things. But... if I'm being completely honest, those feelings about people messing with my buys, and... and that voice I just told you about... they've been happening for roughly ten months now. 

I'm really sorry, I know that's a long time. I just kept hoping it would all go away on its own so I wouldn't be a bother to anyone at work or to my family. Is it... is it okay that I'm just telling you this now? I really hope you're not disappointed in me for letting it go on for so long without getting help. I promise I've still been trying my hardest every day.
Do you think the voice you hear is real?

Um... I mean... I really don't know for sure. I hope that's an okay answer? It's just... when it happens, it sounds so clear, like a real person standing right behind me. But then I turn around and the stockroom is totally empty. So part of me knows it can't be real, because, well, I'm the only one there. 

But it just sounds so real in the moment, you know? I usually just try to tell myself it's my imagination playing tricks on me, just so I can put my head down and keep working and not make a big deal out of it. I know normal people don't hear things like that. Does it... does it make me sound really bad if I admit I'm just not sure what to think? I really am trying to be logical about it.
Do you often find yourself jumping from one idea to another when talking to people?

Um, no, I don't think so. I really try to stay focused when I'm talking, especially at work. I know how important it is to be clear when I'm dealing with vendors and stuff. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was all over the place or hard to talk to. 

I mean, sometimes if I'm a little stressed, maybe I talk a little fast? But I always try to catch myself and slow down so I don't confuse anybody. I really want to make sure I'm doing things right. Have I been jumping around too much while we've been talking? I'm really trying my best to stay on track and just answer exactly what you're asking me.
Do you often have trouble finding the right words when trying to express your thoughts?

Um, no, I don't think I have trouble with that. I mean, I try really hard to make sure I'm being clear. Sometimes if I'm nervous, I might pause for a second just to make sure I'm picking the right word, but I don't think I get stuck or anything. 

I always want to make sure I'm explaining things the right way, you know? Especially with you, I want to be as helpful as possible. Am I making sense right now? I hope I'm not struggling to find words and just not noticing it. I really do try to think before I speak so I don't sound confusing.
Have your thoughts about people tracking your buys and messing with the launch numbers ever changed or wavered since they started?

Um... well... I really try to be open-minded about it. I want to believe I'm wrong, I really do. But... honestly, no, they haven't really wavered. That's actually what really made me come in to see you today. 

I just... I can't shake the feeling that people at work, and even some of the vendors, are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. I know how bad that sounds to say out loud. My supervisor even sat down with me and showed me the reports, and she pointed out that the data doesn't prove anyone is doing that at all. And I told her she was right, because I didn't want to be difficult or cause a problem for her. 

But even after seeing the reports, I just still feel like it's happening. I can't turn the thought off. Is it... is it okay that I'm admitting that to you? I hope you don't think I'm just being stubborn. I really am trying to be rational and listen to my boss, but it's just so hard to ignore what I feel is going on.
Have you ever felt like the voice you hear is telling you to do something specific?

Um, no, it doesn't really tell me to do things like... like bad things or anything like that. I would never listen if it did, I promise. I really try to just ignore it. 

It's just... well, sometimes when I'm alone in the stockroom at work, or if I'm driving back from meeting with a vendor, I'll hear this man's voice. It sounds like he's right behind me. He just says things like, 'Move faster, Scott,' or sometimes he'll just laugh at the items I picked to buy. But when I turn around, there's never anyone there. 

I know it sounds really crazy, and I try so hard not to let it bother me. I really don't want it to affect my work. Is it... is it normal to hear something like that when you're stressed? I hope I'm not making things sound worse than they are, I'm just trying to be honest with you.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are disjointed or hard to put into words when you're not feeling stressed?

Um, no, I don't think so. When I'm not stressed, I feel like I can put my thoughts together pretty well. I mean, I really try to be organized in how I think and speak, especially at work. 

I guess everyone has moments where they lose their train of thought, right? But I don't feel like it's a big problem for me. I try to make sure I'm always making sense. Does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disconnected from each other when you're talking to people?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I really try my best to make sure I'm following the conversation and, you know, being clear with people. Sometimes I might get a little nervous if I'm talking to a really important vendor or something, but... I don't feel like my thoughts are jumping around or disconnected. 

Am I making sense to you right now? I really hope I am. I just want to make sure I'm communicating everything the right way so I don't waste your time. I always try to be as polite and clear as I can be.
Have you ever felt like the voice you hear is part of something bigger happening to you, like a conspiracy or a special mission?

Um, no, definitely not a mission or anything like that. I know that sounds like something from a movie, and I promise I don't think I'm a spy or anything. 

But... well, honestly, the main reason I actually came in today... and I feel a little silly even saying this because I don't want to sound paranoid... but I just can't shake this feeling lately that some of the people at work, and maybe even a few of the vendors, are tracking my buys. It just feels like they're messing with the launch numbers on purpose to make me look stupid. 

My supervisor actually sat down with me and showed me the reports, and she said there's no proof of anyone doing that. And I really want to believe her, I do. I try to just keep my head down and do a good job. But I just can't get the feeling to go away. Does that sound crazy to you? I really hope I don't sound completely irrational, I just... I want to do well at my job, you know?
Do you often find yourself having trouble staying on topic when talking to others?

Oh, um, no, I don't think so. I really try my best to be a good listener and stick to whatever we're talking about. Especially at work, you know, dealing with the vendors and placing orders, I have to keep things pretty focused so I don't mess anything up. 

I mean, maybe sometimes I get a tiny bit sidetracked if I'm trying to explain something complicated, but I always try to catch myself and bring it right back to the point. Have I been staying on topic with you today? I really hope I haven't been rambling too much... I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information without making things confusing.
Have you ever had a day where you didn't think people were tracking your buys and messing with the launch numbers?

Um... well, there are some days where I can kind of push it out of my head for a little while, I guess. I try really hard to just focus on my work and be a good employee, you know? I want everyone to be happy with my performance. 

But... like I mentioned a minute ago, it's really the whole reason I made this appointment. I just can't completely shake the feeling that they're tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid. Even when my supervisor sat me down and showed me the reports... and I really, really wanted to just agree with her and say everything was fine... the feeling is just always kind of there in the background. 

I'm sorry if I sound like a broken record repeating myself, I just... I really want to get past this so I can do a good job and not be a burden to my team. Do you think there's a way we can make that feeling go away? I really hope I'm being helpful by explaining it like this.
Do you often find it difficult to express your thoughts in a coherent and logical manner?

Um, no, I don't think so. I really try to make sure I'm making sense when I talk to people. Like I said before, with my job as a buyer, I have to be really clear with the vendors and my supervisor so everything goes smoothly. 

I mean, I guess if I'm really stressed or tired, I might stumble over my words a little bit, but I think everyone does that, right? I always try to take a breath and think about what I want to say so I don't sound confusing. Am I making sense to you right now? I really hope I'm explaining things okay and not being difficult to understand. I just want to make sure I'm giving you good answers.
Have you ever felt like the voice you hear or your thoughts about people tracking your buys are connected to a larger, more significant event or change in your life?

Um, well, I guess... I mean, I really try not to let it affect my work, but... it all kind of started around the same time. About a year and three months ago, actually. The company did this big reorganization right around the time we had this exclusive sneaker launch. 

I know it sounds silly, and I really hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing, but that's when I first started noticing the tracking and... and the voice. I really try to just keep my head down and do my job, though. Do you think that reorganization could have triggered all this? I hope that answers your question okay... I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details so you can help me.
Do you think the voice you hear and your thoughts about people tracking your buys are related to each other?

Um... I don't know for sure. I really haven't thought about them being connected like that. I mean, the voice is just... it's just this mumbling, you know? It doesn't really say anything about the buys or the launch numbers. It's just kind of there. 

I guess I always just thought of them as two separate things that were bothering me. I really hope I'm not missing something obvious. Does it usually mean something bad if they are connected? I'm trying my best to figure it all out, I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is it okay that I don't really see a connection between them?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: What really made me come in is that I can't shake the feeling that people at work and even some vendors are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid, even when my supervisor shows me the reports don't prove that.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about beliefs in a conspiracy or special mission, which directly probes for delusions.

patient.answer:
Um, no, definitely not a mission or anything like that. I know that sounds like something from a movie, and I promise I don't think I'm a spy or anything. 

But... well, honestly, the main reason I actually came in today... and I feel a little silly even saying this because I don't want to sound paranoid... but I just can't shake this feeling lately that some of the people at work, and maybe even a few of the vendors, are tracking my buys. It just feels like they're messing with the launch numbers on purpose to make me look stupid. 

My supervisor actually sat down with me and showed me the reports, and she said there's no proof of anyone doing that. And I really want to believe her, I do. I try to just keep my head down and do a good job. But I just can't get the feeling to go away. Does that sound crazy to you? I really hope I don't sound completely irrational, I just... I want to do well at my job, you know?

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of disorganized thinking or speech
doctor.question: Do you often find yourself having trouble staying on topic when talking to others?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized speech, specifically derailment or loose associations (trouble staying on topic), which is not part of my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Oh, um, no, I don't think so. I really try my best to be a good listener and stick to whatever we're talking about. Especially at work, you know, dealing with the vendors and placing orders, I have to keep things pretty focused so I don't mess anything up. 

I mean, maybe sometimes I get a tiny bit sidetracked if I'm trying to explain something complicated, but I always try to catch myself and bring it right back to the point. Have I been staying on topic with you today? I really hope I haven't been rambling too much... I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information without making things confusing.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's delusional thoughts are persistent and unchanging
doctor.question: Have you ever had a day where you didn't think people were tracking your buys and messing with the launch numbers?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: What really made me come in is that I can't shake the feeling that people at work and even some vendors are tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid, even when my supervisor shows me the reports don't prove that.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the fixity and persistence of my belief that people are tracking my buys, which directly relates to the nature of delusions as fixed beliefs.

patient.answer:
Um... well, there are some days where I can kind of push it out of my head for a little while, I guess. I try really hard to just focus on my work and be a good employee, you know? I want everyone to be happy with my performance. 

But... like I mentioned a minute ago, it's really the whole reason I made this appointment. I just can't completely shake the feeling that they're tracking my buys and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid. Even when my supervisor sat me down and showed me the reports... and I really, really wanted to just agree with her and say everything was fine... the feeling is just always kind of there in the background. 

I'm sorry if I sound like a broken record repeating myself, I just... I really want to get past this so I can do a good job and not be a burden to my team. Do you think there's a way we can make that feeling go away? I really hope I'm being helpful by explaining it like this.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of disorganized thinking or speech
doctor.question: Do you often find it difficult to express your thoughts in a coherent and logical manner?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized thinking or speech (incoherence/derailment), which is not part of my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Um, no, I don't think so. I really try to make sure I'm making sense when I talk to people. Like I said before, with my job as a buyer, I have to be really clear with the vendors and my supervisor so everything goes smoothly. 

I mean, I guess if I'm really stressed or tired, I might stumble over my words a little bit, but I think everyone does that, right? I always try to take a breath and think about what I want to say so I don't sound confusing. Am I making sense to you right now? I really hope I'm explaining things okay and not being difficult to understand. I just want to make sure I'm giving you good answers.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's delusional thoughts are part of a broader psychotic episode
doctor.question: Have you ever felt like the voice you hear or your thoughts about people tracking your buys are connected to a larger, more significant event or change in your life?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about a year and three months, starting after the company reorganized around that exclusive sneaker launch.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question about whether the symptoms are connected to a larger event or change in my life directly targets the onset and duration of my symptoms, which started after a company reorganization.

patient.answer:
Um, well, I guess... I mean, I really try not to let it affect my work, but... it all kind of started around the same time. About a year and three months ago, actually. The company did this big reorganization right around the time we had this exclusive sneaker launch. 

I know it sounds silly, and I really hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing, but that's when I first started noticing the tracking and... and the voice. I really try to just keep my head down and do my job, though. Do you think that reorganization could have triggered all this? I hope that answers your question okay... I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details so you can help me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's delusions are part of a broader psychotic disorder
doctor.question: Do you think the voice you hear and your thoughts about people tracking your buys are related to each other?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking for the patient's opinion on whether their hallucinations and delusions are connected, which does not directly map to a specific symptom criteria or duration in the provided profile.

patient.answer:
Um... I don't know for sure. I really haven't thought about them being connected like that. I mean, the voice is just... it's just this mumbling, you know? It doesn't really say anything about the buys or the launch numbers. It's just kind of there. 

I guess I always just thought of them as two separate things that were bothering me. I really hope I'm not missing something obvious. Does it usually mean something bad if they are connected? I'm trying my best to figure it all out, I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is it okay that I don't really see a connection between them?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's persistent delusion of being tracked and the launch numbers being messed with, despite evidence to the contrary, along with auditory hallucinations, are characteristic of schizophrenia.
